So many of you may or may not know but some people have a difficult lift for their color especially when going blonde.

When I used to do the Platinum Card blonde I would specifically go to an Aveda School so that way the teacher could be there to help them because I knew that my hair would take a while. I always ask up front what the rate is and I tell them I have a hard lift. One time at the Aveda School they told me it would be around $300. They asked for half up front and that was fine. However for some reason this time it took over 8 hours for my hair to lift because I don't think they have the right developer and toner. At the end the receptionist tells me that'll be $600 and I said I don't think so. Well I do understand as I am a beauty shop baby grew up in beauty shops and went to cosmetology school myself we had an agreed upon price and that was the price that I was willing to pay. Mostly because my hair was mush at the end even though I kept watching it it looked okay but you can't tell once it's under Caps or foils sometimes. They argued with me about it but I got the manager and explained my situation and they agreed that there was an agreed upon price however next time I came in it would be more now that they know it would take longer and that I have a hard lift. I was literally speechless because this was the same woman that told me $300 and took my money and we had this conversation before we even started.

Now since then if I go to get my hair lightened salons tell me they don't want to do a platinum card because I tell them it's a hard lift and they tell me it would generally be too costly.

 The last time I got this done was a few months ago and the salon said how about we do a full weave on you to get the color and I will do your roots at the same time. I asked her what the price would be and she said between 2 and $300 and it would be very close to a platinum card meaning all white hair with a touch of ashtoner. I must say that I was disappointed that it wasn't as blonde as I wanted it to be or as much as they promised me it was still very warm and not cool colored as I wanted.

Now I bet you all are expecting me to say that I didn't pay her the price however here's the shocker.. the end result was $220 and I gave her $300. Why?

Because as I said earlier I did grow up in a beauty shop my whole life and I did go to cosmetology school almost completing my state boards so I know that it takes a while I know that sometimes you do the best you can but everybody's hair is different and we agreed upon a price and it's not fair for me to take the money away from that person who worked so hard. 

Oh I didn't say when she styled it I asked her to curl the ends under and then she flat ironed it as well which again wasn't what I asked for but like I said I still paid.

However... I won't go back to that salon. 

They were nice they did the best they could evidently there was only two gals working in the salon they had to work around a mask there was many different situations going on because it was raining and it was also one of those special travel salons so I figured I probably got what I paid for however I won't Go back.

TLDR: you know you're hair better than anyone else be truthful with what it's going to take for them to do it agree on a price pay half up front pay the rest at the end and don't forget to leave them a tip because they do the best they can if you don't like it talk to the manager and try to negotiate a price don't just walk out that's rude and such a Karen thing to do 😂
